title: TRACER: Trajectory Risk Aggregation for Critical Episodes in Agentic Reasoning
claim: Sparse critical episodes in a long interaction trajectory are turned into step-level signals, then aggregated by a tail-focused risk score.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; dialogue trajectory on left feeds stacked pipeline boxes on right
description: The figure has two panels. On the left, titled 'Multi-Turn Agent–User Interaction Trajectory', is a vertical chat transcript between a user and an agent about mobile data not working. User turns are blue boxes, agent turns are green, tool calls and returns are orange, and a final annotation is purple. A long arrow runs down the left edge to show time. Arrows from selected turns point right into the second panel, 'TRACER Risk Computation Pipeline', which is a stack of four rounded boxes connected by downward arrows. The first box lists step-wise signals (surprisal, repetition, action–observation mismatch, coordination gap) with small icons and a 'spike at roaming failure' callout. The second box shows the MAX-composite step risk formula above a bar chart with red spikes. The third box shows top-K mean and ℓ∞ aggregation with mini bar charts. The last box gives the final TRACER score formula. The eye goes first to the colorful dialogue on the left, then follows the arrows into the equations on the right.
caption: Overview of TRACER for trajectory-level uncertainty estimation in agentic reasoning. Left: A multi-turn Agent– User interaction with tool calls and delayed failure resolution. Right: At each agent step t, content-aware surprisal Ut, agent repetition Da(t), action–observation mismatch DA
abstract: Estimating uncertainty for AI agents in real-world multi-turn tool-using interaction with humans is difficult because failures are often triggered by sparse critical episodes (e.g., looping, incoherent tool use, or user-agent miscoordination) even when local generation appears confident. Existing uncertainty proxies focus on single-shot text generation and therefore miss these trajectory-level breakdown signals. We introduce TRACER, a trajectory-level uncertainty metric for dual-control Tool-Agent-User interaction. TRACER combines content-aware surprisal with situational-awareness signals, semantic and lexical repetition, and tool-grounded coherence gaps, and aggregates them using a tail-focused risk functional with a MAX-composite step risk to surface decisive anomalies. We evaluate TRACER on $Ï^2$-bench by predicting task failure and selective task execution. To this end, TRACER improves AUROC by up to 37.1% and AUARC by up to 55% over baselines, enabling earlier and more accurate detection of uncertainty in complex conversational tool-use settings. Our code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/sinatayebati/agent-tracer.
